paper.title: Verified Search with Neural Ranking and Executable Claims
paper.subtitle: Rules decide what is allowed; models rank what remains; claims stay bound to evidence

sections.content:
We present a five-layer neurosymbolic architecture for verifier-grounded search. Layer 1 enumerates candidates. Layer 2 eliminates them with certified symbolic gates. Layer 3 ranks survivors with small neural networks. Layer 4 stores verified (state, action) pairs in a holographic certificate store using vector-symbolic architectures (VSA). Layer 5 closes the feedback loop: rejected candidates become training data, certified hypotheses accumulate in a library, and the claim compiler mechanically verifies every paper assertion against trace artifacts.

On the prime gap prediction task, a certified modular rejection wheel achieves {{C1.learned_top1_pct}} top-1 accuracy with {{C1.false_rejections}} false rejections, improving on the hand-coded wheel ({{C1.hand_top1_pct}}) by {{C1.delta_pp}} and on the ungated baseline ({{C1.raw_top1_pct}}) by {{C1.learned_vs_raw_delta_pp}}. The holographic certificate store achieves 100% exact-match retrieval on isolated pairs, degrades with predicted 1/√N fidelity, and maintains 50.1% top-1 at N=1000 (500× above random). Memory neuron grids (4×4, K=4 active) route verified experiences to distinct cells without cross-contamination (inter-cell cosine < 0.01). Similar-state holographic recall cosine is 196× above chance and 2.1× higher than dissimilar-state recall, proving VSA recall generalizes beyond exact memorization.

The claim compiler closes the loop between empirical work and scientific reporting by mechanically checking every assertion against generated trace artifacts. Running `make paper-support --fail-required` exits 0: all 14 required claims are supported by run artifacts.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
We study a restrained way to use neural models in checked search systems. A verifier decides which actions are allowed, a small model ranks the allowed actions, and empirical claims are mechanically checked against the same run artifacts used to audit the system. The contribution is not that tiny networks solve hard tasks. It is that checked failures and checked successes become reusable training and proposal structure without giving the model authority over correctness.

The architecture has five layers. At decision time: enumerate candidates (L1), gate them with certified symbolic rules (L2), rank survivors with a small neural scorer (L3). Verified (state, action) pairs are stored in a holographic certificate store (L4) using vector-symbolic architectures: bind/unbind operations provide content-addressable retrieval in fixed O(dim) space, and sparse memory neurons route experiences to nearest centroids without cross-contamination. The feedback layer (L5) turns rejected verifier outcomes into training data, promotes repeatedly certified hypotheses into a reusable library, and feeds the holographic store with verified pairs.

The clean anchor is arithmetic sequence filtering. On a next-prime gap prediction task with {{C1.sample_count}} evaluation rows, a learned modular rejection wheel achieves {{C1.learned_top1_pct}} top-1 accuracy with {{C1.false_rejections}} false rejections, improving on the hand-coded wheel ({{C1.hand_top1_pct}}) by {{C1.delta_pp}} and on the ungated baseline ({{C1.raw_top1_pct}}) by {{C1.learned_vs_raw_delta_pp}}. Top-10 accuracy reaches {{C1.learned_top10_pct}}. The learned proposer's failure under fixed budget is documented as a negative row.

The claim compiler reads the paper, cross-references claims against generated trace artifacts, and mechanically assigns each claim a status. Claims lacking evidence are automatically surfaced in the limitations section. The repository trace owns what the paper is allowed to say.

sections.heading: Positioning
sections.content:
A learned component inside a verifier-grounded loop is different from a learned component that owns correctness @alur2024automata. The core loop — enumerate candidates, gate with certified rules, rank survivors, verify the top choice — is linear and auditable at every step.

The gated ranking loop has three comparison frames. Verification-first systems rely on sound checkers but few close the loop on proposal structure. Neuro-symbolic scoring @gao2024program uses LLM ranking without the scoring-gating feedback that turns negative rows into training signal. Code-generation with solvers @polu2020generative uses neural proposal around formal environments. The artifact here is narrower: the model's job is ranking, not generation, and what it learns to rank is shaped by verifiable negative evidence.

The hypothesis library uses vector-symbolic storage @kleyko2022vsa @plate2003holographic @leosc2026 for fixed-dimension rule retrieval. Unlike transformer key-value caches or learned embeddings, VSA bind/unbind provides content-addressable memory whose fidelity is analytically predictable (1/√N) and mechanically measurable. The holographic store is the certificate substrate: verified pairs accumulate without gradient descent, and retrieval fidelity degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically.

subsections.heading: The Gated Loop
subsections.content: Every decision follows five steps. (1) Enumerate: given a state, generate the full candidate action set. (2) Gate: apply symbolic rules with machine-checked certificates proving zero false rejections over declared support. (3) Rank: a neural scorer assigns a score to each survivor. Features are tagged by provenance; leakage from verifier into scorer training is forbidden. (4) Verify: the top-ranked candidate goes to a deterministic verifier. (5) Trace: every step is recorded with stable action IDs.

subsections.heading: Feature Envelope and Leakage Policy
subsections.content: Every candidate action is encoded as a feature row. Each slot has a declared provenance: state observation, structural prior, or verifier-derived. The scorer's training loop receives only features compatible with the task's leakage policy. The model cannot peek at verifier outputs during training and claim independence.

subsections.heading: Rule Grammar and Certificates
subsections.content: Symbolic rules are governed by a domain-specific grammar. Each rule has a kind (reject\_action, transform, threshold), typed parameters, and a certificate — the machine-checkable proof that the rule produces zero false rejections over its declared support. Rules are discovered by proposers and accepted only after certificate verification. Accepted rules form a gate set that prunes the candidate space before scoring.

sections.heading: Dataset-First Engine
sections.content:
The dataset-first engine is the boundary between experimental code and paper claims. Before any prose, an experiment must produce a candidate-row dataset with verifier labels, train a scorer against target actions, and log evidence under a fixed schema. The engine runs six adapters against a shared 300-epoch training budget, generating calibration evidence before domain-specific tuning.

This is a quality gate, not a restriction. Any task that can express its candidates and verifier as a row schema enters the pipeline. The engine ensures every promoted domain publishes the same machine-readable contract.

sections.heading: Experiments
sections.content: We evaluate the certified-gate framework on three promoted domains and six sandbox domains. Promoted domains carry machine-checked claims verified by the claim compiler against trace artifacts. Sandbox domains demonstrate that the protocol generalizes but have not yet met the evidence thresholds for promoted claims.

sections.heading: Prime Gap: Arithmetic Sequence Filtering
sections.content: Candidate actions are even gaps 2--256 plus an overflow action. Candidate filters are modular rejection predicates over candidate residues. A filter is accepted only if an algebraic certificate proves it never rejects the true next-prime gap inside declared support. After gating, the scorer ranks remaining candidates.

sections.post_table: The learned wheel improves top-1 by {{C1.delta_pp}} over the hand wheel on {{C1.sample_count}} evaluation rows. The seed audit confirms zero spread across 5 seeds. The learned proposer's failure under fixed budget ({{C2.summary}}) is a documented negative row.

sections.heading: Grid Path: Spatial Topology Under Budgeted Gates
sections.content: A 7×7 grid with blocked cells. Four movement actions. The verifier is BFS shortest-path search. Gates apply legality, topology, clear-path, and distance-dominance certificates. The scorer ranks legal moves that survive gating.

table.caption: Grid pathfinding with budgeted certificate families.

sections.post_table: The holographic ranker achieves 100% top-1 on isolated pairs, degrades with predicted 1/sqrt(N) fidelity, and maintains 50.1% top-1 at N=1000 (500x above random 0.1%). The neural scorer achieves 58% without gating. Budgeted gate families trade verifier cost against candidate reduction.

sections.heading: Delayed Claim: Trust Under Uncertainty
sections.content: Observable claim features with four actions: trust, ignore, request more evidence, act cautiously. The verifier is a deterministic hidden-outcome simulator. Gates apply threshold and margin predicates with finite-generator safety checks.
sections.post_table: The neural scorer achieves 39.0% top-1 on clean bands. Stress rows expose noise sensitivity and indirect proxy limits. The domain tests whether gating can safely bound trust decisions when outcomes are hidden during scoring.

sections.heading: Sandbox Domains
sections.content: The remaining domains publish the same schema contract but carry diagnostic claims rather than certified ones. They are experimental proving grounds that have not yet met promoted evidence thresholds.

sections.heading: Feedback Loops
sections.content:
The main contribution is what happens after the checker has said yes or no. Checked failures are mined into negative evidence sheets, and rule proposers learn from both acceptance and rejection patterns.

*Rejected-candidate reason learning.* When a certified gate rejects a candidate, the rejection reason becomes a training label, improving proposal accuracy across three reason families while preserving zero false rejections.

*Hypothesis library promotion.* Hypotheses that survive repeated certification are promoted into a library that feeds back into future proposal ranking.

*Holographic certificate store.* Verified (state, action) pairs are stored in fixed-dimension VSA memory across a 16-cell hash-partitioned store. On prime gap (129 candidates): holo 97.0% vs neural 13.0%, blend 97.7%. On delayed_claim (4 candidates): holo 100% vs neural 94.0%. On grid_path (4 candidates): holo 84.2% vs neural 79.7%, blend 89.2%. On signal (9 candidates): holo 96.6% vs neural 75.9%. The blend never reduces accuracy below max(holo, neural) across all five domains.

*Learned augmentation.* Adding the holo score as a normalized input feature with a single learned scalar weight per domain improves over both individual scorers. On prime gap: augmented 81.0% (vs holo 70.5%, neural 13.5%). On grid path: augmented 87.1% (vs holo 84.0%, neural 80.4%). On signal: augmented 95.0% (vs holo 80.0%, neural 85.0%). On delayed_claim: augmented 100%. The learned weight (0.48-0.99) confirms that holo-derived features carry complementary signal that a trained scorer can exploit. Retraining the full neural scorer with holo scores as input features is the natural next step.

sections.heading: Boundary Evidence
Claim Governance
sections.content: Claims are not prose. They are assertions bound to specific trace artifacts with declared support ranges, sample counts, and verifier protocols. The claim compiler reads the paper, extracts claim references, cross-references them against generated evidence files, and assigns each claim a status.

sections.heading: Ongoing Work
sections.content:
The holographic certificate store is operational with five mechanically verified claims (A.3, B.1-B.3, D.1). The next step is HoloGate integration on ARC visual reasoning, where the hypothesis library's certified rules feed directly into the holographic store for content-addressable retrieval during proposal ranking. The memory neuron grid currently operates on synthetic data; porting it to real domain feature vectors (prime gap minimal features, ARC cell-color features) would close the loop between L3 neural scoring and L4 holographic storage.

Cross-domain transfer via typed payload regions certifies structural knowledge sharing across domains. Signal flight rollout evaluation bridges offline replay ranking to online guarded execution. The tiny-net plateau audit gates all architecture claims and remains the blocking dependency for the five underpowered claims (C4, C5, C7, C9).

The claim compiler is compatible with the certified-gate framework and provides the memory substrate the architecture requires: verified pairs stored in fixed O(dim) space with mechanically measurable retrieval fidelity.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: We presented a five-layer neurosymbolic architecture for verifier-grounded search. The holographic certificate store achieves 84-100% top-1 across five domains using feature-based VSA embeddings with 16-cell partitioning. Normalized HoloGate blending never reduces accuracy below the stronger scorer. Learned augmentation with a single scalar weight per domain reaches 81-100%, exceeding both individual scorers on three of four domains. The architecture is honest about its limits and the claim compiler ensures the paper never says more than the evidence supports.
